ECC-DCH-3018-1.1.title:

procedures (Beginning Pre-school Teacher)
ECC-DCH-3018-1.1.description:
This skill describes the ability to ensure a safe and healthy physical
environment for children by following regulations regarding basic health,
hygiene, and safety. It includes adherence to procedures for illnesses,
accidents and emergencies, promoting healthy eating habits of children
by ensuring a balanced diet and teaching and modelling good nutrition,
hygiene and safety practices. It also involves communicating openly with
colleagues, families and professionals with regard to health and safety
matters, and keeping up-to-date on safe care giving practices.

accidents and emergencies, as well as health, nutrition, hygiene, and
safety standards to ensure a safe and healthy physical environment for
children. It includes ensuring quality and timely care-giving practices to
meet the needs of each child, promoting healthy eating habits of children,
as well as identifying and reporting suspected emotional distress, abuse
and neglect of children in appropriate ways. It involves teaching and
modelling good nutrition, hygiene and safety practices, as well as
communicating with families and colleagues the importance of these
practices

child by utilising observations and documentations of children’s learning
and development , to develop appropriate activities and create an
environment that is conducive to teaching and learning. It includes
responding to questions from colleagues and families about children’s
behaviour, maintaining confidentiality of young children and their families

documentation techniques adopted.

practice by applying understanding of developmental stages of children

open-ended learning environments to support children’s learning and
interests. It includes assisting in the preparation and provision of
materials to support the development of quality learning environments,
the collaboration with colleagues to design and set up learning

regular routines and programmes that are flexible and adaptable to
children’s temperaments and interests.

Demonstrate ethical behaviour and professionalism (Beginning Preschool
Teacher)
ECC-BPC-3004-1.1.description:
This skill describes the ability to engage in professional responsibilities
that contribute toward the success of children, families and programmes
in adherence to the core values as espoused in the AECES Code of
Ethics. This includes maintaining professional boundaries and
demonstrating ethical conduct in interactions with children, families,
colleagues and community stakeholders. It also involves being
accountable and responsible for own actions, and reflecting and
improving on one’s own practice

values (Beginning Pre-school Teacher)
ECC-BOC-3006-1.1.description:
This skill describes the ability to demonstrate and uphold the centre’s
vision, mission and values through maintaining professional ethics in
daily practice. It also includes articulating the centre’s rationale to various
stakeholders, developing a personal set of beliefs and values as an
educator and sharing feedback to ensure the relevance of the vision,
mission and values.

centre’s vision, mission and values. It also includes understanding the
importance of professional ethics, and developing a core set of beliefs
and values as an early childhood educator that is aligned to the
centre’s vision, mission and values.

ECC-DCH-2006-1.1.title:
Display sensitivity to each child’s needs (within a group setting)
through respectful, responsive and reciprocal interactions and
relationships with children
ECC-DCH-2006-1.1.description:
This skill describes the ability to demonstrate sensitivity to each child’s
needs through respectful, responsive and reciprocal interactions and
relationships with children. It includes supporting children’s needs by
responding sensitively to their verbal and non-verbal communication,
feelings, ideas and behaviours, creating a nurturing environment, giving
attention to and demonstrating familiarity with each child and using
positive guidance techniques to acknowledge and affirm each child’s
personal efforts. It also involves practising regular open communication,
managing own emotional responses towards children, and reflecting on
own effectiveness in identifying and applying the appropriate positive
guidance techniques to support children’s emotional development.

display sensitivity, maintain confidentiality, and exercise empathy when

ECC-DCH-3016-1.1.title:
Foster trusting, respectful relationships with children through
positive interactions with them
ECC-DCH-3016-1.1.description:
This skill describes the ability to foster trusting, respectful relationships
with children by demonstrating understanding of and respect towards
children of different temperaments and culture. This includes creating a
nurturing emotional and interactional environment that promotes security
and attachment for children through prompt, appropriate and consistent
responses to the needs of each child, as well as using positive guidance
techniques to acknowledge and affirm each child’s personal efforts. It
also includes management of own emotional responses towards children
to provide respectful and responsive care-giving, collaboration with
families, and self-reflection of own effectiveness in identifying and
applying appropriate positive guidance techniques to support children’s
emotional development.

previous.title: Interaction and Relationship
previous.description: Develop trusting and respectful relationships with children

updated.title: Interaction and Relationship
updated.description: Develop trusting and respectful relationships with children

ECC-DCH-3017-1.1.title:
Guide the development and enhancement of self-awareness, selfregulation,
social awareness and confidence in children
ECC-DCH-3017-1.1.description:
This skill describes the ability to use appropriate strategies to guide the
development and enhancement of self-awareness, self-regulation, social
awareness and confidence in children, based on the understanding of
developmental stages of each child and theories of social and emotional
development. It includes guiding children in the understanding and
identification of their own strengths, likes and dislikes, and needs. It also
includes providing appropriate opportunities for children to make
informed choices about matters that affect them, model recognition and
expression of feelings, assisting children in identifying and expressing
their feelings in appropriate ways, guiding children in recognising the
feelings and perspectives of others, appreciating diversity and showing
respect for others, motivating children to succeed when faced with
challenges and demonstrating support for children who require guidance
in managing distress.

previous.title: Interaction and Relationship
previous.description: Develop trusting and respectful relationships with children

updated.title: Interaction and Relationship
updated.description: Develop trusting and respectful relationships with children

learning environment.

Support children’s development of secure attachments through
warm, consistent and nurturing caregiving (Infant/Beginning
Educarer)
ECC-DCH-2007-1.1.description:
This skill describes the ability to support children’s development of secure
attachments by responding promptly, appropriately and consistently to
children’s needs and demonstrating positive interactions with children. It
includes creating daily opportunities for interactions with each child, using
care-giving activities to foster healthy development of secure attachment,
maintaining regular and predictable yet flexible routines and
programmes. It involves collaborating with colleagues to ensure the
provision of continuity of care for children, and reflecting on own
effectiveness in supporting children’s development of secure attachment.
